plan: My value is $29. Since this is the only round, I want to win if my bid is likely to exceed the second highest bid. A conservative approach is to bid slightly above the midpoint of the possible value range (0-20), anticipating others will bid lower. However, my value is quite high, so I can be more aggressive. I will bid $19.50. This ensures I win against any bid below $19.50, and my profit will be substantial even if the second highest bid is close to $20.

My value is $27. Since this is the only round, I want to maximize my expected profit. I'll consider the worst-case scenarios. If I bid $27, I win if I'm the highest, paying the second highest bid. If I bid lower, I might lose to a bid slightly above mine. I'll bid slightly above my value, hoping to win against potentially high bids, but not excessively so as to overpay. A bid of $20.5 seems reasonable.

My value is $25. Since this is the only round, I want to maximize my expected profit. I'll bid aggressively, but not at my full value. I need to consider the potential for overpaying. A bid slightly above the maximum possible value for others ($20) seems reasonable. I'll bid $20.1 to almost guarantee a win, paying a maximum of $20. This yields a minimum profit of $25 - $20 = $5.
